title: Saylor Says Strategy, Strive Can Win Share of $318.5T With Bitcoin
summary: Bitcoin finance is competing for allocations within global equity and debt markets totaling $318.5 trillion, according to Michael Saylor. He argues that responsible rivals can strengthen shared demand, improve funding conditions, and attract more investors. Saylor Looks Beyond Rivals to Global Capit...
content:
Bitcoin finance is competing for allocations within global equity and debt markets totaling $318.5 trillion, according to Michael Saylor. He argues that responsible rivals can strengthen shared demand, improve funding conditions, and attract more investors.

Key Takeaways

  • Saylor places bitcoin finance within a $318.5 trillion market backdrop.
  • Asset gains, cheaper funding, and equity valuations could reinforce growth.
  • Strive’s $50 million STRC purchase illustrates cooperation among rivals.

Saylor Looks Beyond Rivals to Global Capital Markets

Investors could gain more choices as competing bitcoin treasury companies develop income and growth securities, Michael Saylor contends. The founder and executive chairman of Strategy Inc. (Nasdaq: MSTR), a bitcoin treasury company, shared his argument on X Sept. 30. Saylor said: “I want Strive to succeed. I want every well-managed issuer of bitcoin-powered Digital Credit to succeed.”

The opportunity extends into established markets, where even small allocations could represent substantial sums for the category. The Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA) recorded $157.8 trillion in global equity capitalization and $160.7 trillion in fixed-income debt outstanding at year-end 2025. Together, they total $318.5 trillion. Saylor wrote: “One tenth of one percent of either market is roughly $160 billion.”

He added:

“That is the scale against which we should measure our opportunity. Bitcoin treasury equities and bitcoin-powered credit are young categories seeking recognition within much larger markets.”

Saylor distinguishes bitcoin for long-term allocations, preferred stocks for income, and treasury-company common shares for growth capital. He classifies STRC and SATA, issued by Strategy and bitcoin treasury company Strive Inc. (Nasdaq: ASST), respectively, as digital credit. These bitcoin-based income securities prioritize dividends over common shares but do not automatically provide secured claims on bitcoin.

Bitcoin Gains and Cheaper Funding Could Reinforce Growth

Newly financed acquisitions add demand for an asset with constrained issuance, potentially benefiting every company holding it. Bitcoin’s supply limit underpins Saylor’s first growth driver: appreciation that strengthens asset coverage and financing capacity. Individual purchases cannot guarantee higher prices. He stated: “The value created by broader bitcoin adoption can reach every balance sheet built on bitcoin.”

Broader acceptance of preferred-stock products could improve funding terms as investors become familiar with their structures and risks. Saylor’s STRC income model could benefit from analyst coverage, institutional research, trading infrastructure, and distribution. Greater confidence may narrow financing spreads, the extra return demanded above benchmark rates, though changing interest rates could offset savings.

Higher equity valuations could enable capital raising, further acquisitions, or retirement of costly obligations, completing a potentially reinforcing cycle. Strategy’s $152 million STRC repurchase, disclosed Sept. 28, illustrates active balance-sheet management. Growth must exceed funding costs and dilution, which reduces existing shareholders’ proportional ownership. Bitcoin pays no interest, so any margin between asset returns and financing costs depends on uncertain appreciation and disciplined execution.

Strive Shows How Competitors Can Become Customers

Cooperation already extends to investment decisions, with Strive allocating part of its treasury to Strategy’s preferred stock. It disclosed a $50 million purchase of STRC on March 11, representing 500,000 shares. Saylor cites this as evidence that rivals can become customers while maintaining independent management and financing decisions.

The firm’s subsequent expansion illustrates how preferred-stock financing can support accumulation of the same underlying asset held by competitors. Strive disclosed 1,107 additional bitcoin acquired for $94.5 million Sept. 28, bringing holdings to 27,462 bitcoin. CEO Matt Cole attributed 85% of total capital raised, including warrant proceeds, to SATA.

Saylor compares complementary businesses to Ford and the oil industry, extending his ecosystem to payments and derivatives, financial contracts for managing risk. Multiple issuers could accommodate institutional exposure limits, though diversification preserves common bitcoin risk. Weak operators can damage confidence, while falling prices, wider spreads, and lower valuations can reinforce losses. He identifies sound capitalization, prudent liquidity, and transparent disclosures as conditions for responsible growth.

The Strategy executive chairman concluded:

“When we build on bitcoin, we have an interest in one another’s success. Let’s build the industry together.”

title: Grayscale: XRP’s Near-6% Bitcoin Valuation Sets a Benchmark for Zcash
summary: XRP is valued at nearly 6% of bitcoin’s market capitalization, a level Grayscale cites as context for how far rival digital currencies can grow. Zcash rose from under 0.1% to about 1.5% of bitcoin’s value in a year, and the firm says it has not hit a valuation ceiling. XRP, Zcash, and Litecoin Share...
content:
XRP is valued at nearly 6% of bitcoin’s market capitalization, a level Grayscale cites as context for how far rival digital currencies can grow. Zcash rose from under 0.1% to about 1.5% of bitcoin’s value in a year, and the firm says it has not hit a valuation ceiling.

Key Takeaways

  • Grayscale counts 10 qualifying tokens alongside bitcoin in its sector.
  • XRP’s market value approaches 6% of bitcoin’s, versus Zcash’s 1.5%.
  • The firm argues that ZEC has not reached a valuation ceiling.

XRP, Zcash, and Litecoin Share Bitcoin’s Currency Category

Digital currency competition extends beyond bitcoin (BTC) to 10 other qualifying tokens, including XRP, Zcash (ZEC), and Litecoin (LTC), according to Grayscale. Zach Pandl, head of research at the crypto asset manager, outlined their shared classification in a Sept. 29 analysis. The firm’s Currencies Crypto Sector groups blockchains focused on the digital currency use case.

The category encompasses monetary functions such as transferring value, storing value, and expressing prices in a common unit. These digital currency functions span standard monetary protocols and cryptocurrencies with privacy features. FTSE Russell, an index provider, and Grayscale review the sectors and their constituents quarterly, allowing classifications to change as the market develops. Pandl wrote: “Bitcoin is the king of the category.”

Litecoin illustrates how a decentralized payment network enables direct transfers between users rather than relying on a central processor. Its peer-to-peer digital currency supports payments worldwide. The network launched in 2011 and operates through open-source software. That payment function complements the confidential transactions emphasized in the analyst’s discussion of ZEC.

Grayscale included a chart in its Sept. 29 analysis comparing 10 cryptocurrencies’ market capitalizations with bitcoin’s, using 30-day averages through Sept. 28. Market capitalization measures a cryptocurrency’s circulating supply multiplied by its price. The chart shows XRP above the other nine tokens by relative valuation, while Zcash’s recent rise lifts it above monero (XMR), bitcoin cash, and litecoin. These comparisons measure each token’s market capitalization against bitcoin’s, rather than its share of the entire cryptocurrency market.

XRP’s Near-6% Valuation Frames Zcash’s Growth Potential

XRP currently has a market capitalization approaching 6% of bitcoin’s, providing a larger relative valuation than ZEC in Pandl’s comparison. ZEC’s value increased from less than 0.1% of BTC’s a year earlier to approximately 1.5%, using Artemis analytics data through Sept. 28.

Historical valuations underpin the argument that competing digital currencies can command a larger share of the category than ZEC currently holds. During the 2017-18 market cycle, XRP, bitcoin cash (BCH), litecoin, and dash (DASH) each reached at least 3% of bitcoin’s market capitalization. Pandl describes the recent increase as substantial but consistent with the sector’s history. He argues that the token has not reached a valuation ceiling.

The price appreciation also carries implications for network security through the rewards available to miners who verify transactions. Grayscale’s Sept. 11 estimates put Zcash mining rewards at approximately twice bitcoin’s per machine under specified assumptions. Those figures concern mining revenue; electricity, equipment, and operating expenses determine actual profit.

Privacy Gives Zcash a Distinct Competitive Role

Demand for confidential transactions forms the central basis of the firm’s outlook for further gains in the digital currency category. The token combines bitcoin-like monetary characteristics with privacy features. Cryptographic techniques used by privacy coins conceal transaction details while enabling networks to verify transfers, distinguishing them from cryptocurrencies whose transaction records are publicly traceable.

Interest in financial confidentiality accompanied stronger prices for these assets earlier this year, well before the latest assessment of relative valuations. Zcash reached $600 in early May, marking an earlier stage of the rally. By Sept. 29, its price stood at roughly $1,500, compared with about $60 a year earlier. The researcher attributed the magnitude of that rise to a low starting valuation and a large addressable market.

The broader privacy category expanded, with ZEC accounting for approximately 62% of its market value in blockchain data provider Glassnode’s Sept. 7 snapshot. Pandl’s outlook remains conditional on the cryptocurrency’s competitive capabilities: “If Zcash continues to offer the most effective privacy features among competing cryptocurrencies, we think it can capture additional market share.”

title: CFTC seeks to define event contracts as swaps amid prediction market fight
summary: The classification could assist the CFTC’s claim that it has exclusive federal jurisdiction over event contracts offered on regulated prediction markets.
content:
The classification could assist the CFTC’s claim that it has exclusive federal jurisdiction over event contracts offered on regulated prediction markets.

The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission is seeking to clarify the definition of a “swap” amid a jurisdictional fight with state gambling regulators over prediction markets. 

An Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs docket shows the agency has submitted a proposed rule to expand the definition of “swap” to include event contracts, along with an interim final rule that would exclude casino-style gambling products. Both are under review. 

The classification matters because the CFTC has argued that federal law gives it exclusive authority over swaps traded on its regulated exchanges, such as those offered by Polymarket and Kalshi. US state regulators have disputed that position, particularly for sports event contracts, arguing they are subject to state gambling laws. 

Related: Kalshi loses appeal, setting up potential Supreme Court case

title: Uphold Adds XRP, Bitcoin Inheritance, Citing $331 Billion Stranded
summary: Passing cryptocurrency to an heir requires both legal ownership and a way to authorize transactions. A new service addresses that gap as its provider cites roughly $331 billion in estimated stranded holdings linked to deaths or missing credentials. Uphold Vault Users Get a $19.99 Monthly Inheritance...
content:
Passing cryptocurrency to an heir requires both legal ownership and a way to authorize transactions. A new service addresses that gap as its provider cites roughly $331 billion in estimated stranded holdings linked to deaths or missing credentials.

Key Takeaways

  • The supported holdings are XRP, bitcoin (BTC), and Hedera (HBAR).
  • Beneficiaries remain unable to spend funds until their claims are approved.
  • Current Uphold Vault customers will see new pricing after Dec. 31, 2026.

Uphold Vault Users Get a $19.99 Monthly Inheritance Option

Crypto holders can arrange for a named beneficiary to receive their assets after death through Uphold Vault, an app-based wallet. The financial technology company announced Vault Inheritance Sept. 29. Its assisted self-custody model combines user control with company support for replacing cryptographic keys, the credentials used to authorize transactions.

The feature costs $19.99 per month and includes a free 30-day trial for U.S. users with their subscription. The launch addresses an access problem that can leave families unable to recover cryptocurrency despite inheriting legal ownership. Unlike a conventional investment account, a blockchain balance may remain inaccessible when the deceased owner leaves no usable credentials.

Nancy Beaton, Uphold’s president of consumer, said:

“Uphold Vault Inheritance gives our customers something major players in the industry haven’t offered before: a credible, straightforward way to ensure their crypto goes exactly where they intend it to.”

How Beneficiaries Receive Control of the Assets

Customers begin by inviting a beneficiary from their dashboard, which sends notification and account setup instructions to the designated person. That person establishes an account with the provider to accept the eventual distribution. Customers can change their selection during their lifetime. The company says the beneficiary needs no previous experience with digital currencies.

After the customer’s death, the compliance support team reviews legal documentation before approving a claim and transferring the holdings into the recipient’s wallet. Until approval, the funds remain in the deceased customer’s account. This procedure addresses a practical obstacle illustrated by families losing access to inherited cryptocurrency.

Access arrangements have historically involved passing passwords, personal identification numbers (PINs), and recovery information to a trusted family member. A 2017 account described written instructions and backup seed phrases stored for that purpose. These phrases are sequences of words used to restore a wallet when a device or its login details are unavailable.

How Much Bitcoin Is Actually Lost?

Uphold values nearly 4 million BTC believed to be stranded at approximately $331 billion, including holdings affected by owner deaths or missing credentials. Separately, bitcoin financial services provider River estimated in its research on permanent bitcoin losses that 1.57 million coins were permanently lost, with 98% of those losses occurring before 2020. Its analysis treats a subset of long-inactive coins as likely lost.

Determining how much is permanently inaccessible remains uncertain, as inactive addresses may also belong to long-term holders. Different assumptions about early mining holdings affect estimates of lost coins. A dormant balance might remain spendable by its owner, while a missing private key, the secret credential that authorizes transactions, may prevent anyone from moving it.

Private keys govern spending authority within bitcoin wallets, even when an heir has obtained legal title through an estate. That technical requirement exists separately from ownership records and succession documents. The new arrangement connects a verified claim with the delivery of the cryptographic authority needed to manage the deceased person’s investment.

Vault began in December 2023 with XRP support, followed by bitcoin support in April 2024. Alongside its built-in key replacement, the product provides access to trading on the platform. The latest addition extends those functions to legacy planning, with current customers scheduled to see the revised pricing plan after Dec. 31, 2026.

title: MetaMask exits Ethereum validators amid undisclosed security incident
summary: MetaMask said it is investigating the threat internally and said it has found no immediate threat to its wallets.
content:
MetaMask has announced it is responding to a security incident affecting part of its infrastructure and is exiting affected staking validators as a precaution.

In an update on Wednesday, MetaMask said it was addressing the ongoing threat internally and was working with external partners and security advisors. It did not share what the security issue was but said it has not identified any immediate threat to MetaMask wallets.

MetaMask said the precautionary measures involve validators within its non-custodial staking operations.

Cointelegraph reached out to MetaMask but did not receive an immediate response.

Lido details validator exits and potential penalties

Lido separately said MetaMask Staking had begun taking “precautionary steps to protect client assets related to its operated Ethereum validators,” including exiting its Ether (ETH) validators in the Lido protocol on Wednesday.

The last of the affected validators are expected to exit by the end of Oct. 7.

“ETH exited from MetaMask Staking-operated validators is expected to return to the protocol gradually as the relevant validators complete the exit, withdrawal, and re-entry cycle, which is estimated to take approximately up to 45 days due to the extended entry queue,” said Lido Finance developer Will Shannon.

This is a developing story. More information will be added as it becomes available.

title: MSCI Rule Puts Strategy at Risk, Says Bitcoin Policy Institute Paper
summary: A private index committee that never touches investor cash can still trigger billions of dollars in stock trades. A new Bitcoin Policy Institute paper says MSCI’s proposed test could eject Strategy, Metaplanet, and uranium holder Yellow Cake from major indexes, while an earlier estimate put potentia...
content:
A private index committee that never touches investor cash can still trigger billions of dollars in stock trades. A new Bitcoin Policy Institute paper says MSCI’s proposed test could eject Strategy, Metaplanet, and uranium holder Yellow Cake from major indexes, while an earlier estimate put potential Strategy selling at $2.8 billion from MSCI-linked funds alone. The catch is that MSCI’s new screen hinges on “operating assets,” a category the paper says isn’t defined by U.S. GAAP or IFRS.

Key Takeaways

  • MSCI’s simulated index deletions include Strategy, Metaplanet and Yellow Cake.
  • JPMorgan estimated MSCI removal could trigger $2.8 billion in Strategy selling.
  • Bitcoin Policy Institute says MSCI expects a decision by Oct. 16.

Wall Street’s Quiet Committee Can Move Billions

Your “passive” index fund isn’t quite as passive as the label suggests. Somewhere upstream, a private index provider writes the rules deciding which companies count as the market, and those decisions can send funds scrambling to buy or sell billions of dollars in shares.

On Wednesday, the Washington, D.C.-based, non-partisan, non-profit think tank, Bitcoin Policy Institute, took the wraps off that machinery in a new paper by Executive Director Conner Brown, focusing on MSCI’s proposed test for “non-operating companies.” MSCI’s own simulation, according to the paper, would remove Strategy, Metaplanet, and Yellow Cake, a company holding physical uranium.

Passive Money Still Has Someone Picking the List

Brown’s paper on the subject puts some eye-popping numbers behind the power wielded by index providers. As of July, index funds held $21.8 trillion, or 53.9% of U.S. long-term fund assets, versus $18.6 trillion in actively managed funds. By 2025, index funds owned 19% of the U.S. stock market. MSCI alone says $21 trillion is benchmarked to its indexes, including $2.8 trillion in equity exchange-traded funds that track them directly.

That leads to one of the more counterintuitive points in Brown’s research. The index provider doesn’t actually manage those trillions. Fund managers do. Yet when an index provider changes the companies on its list, funds built to track that benchmark generally have to adjust with it. As Brown’s analysis lays it out, the firm writing the rulebook never touches the investor’s money, but its decisions can still set billions of dollars in motion.

The mechanics became considerably less theoretical in 2025. The Bitcoin Policy Institute author recounts how MSCI proposed excluding companies whose digital assets represented at least 50% of total assets, putting the bitcoin treasury firm Strategy squarely in the frame. JPMorgan analysts estimated Strategy’s removal could prompt roughly $2.8 billion in selling by MSCI-tracking funds, climbing to $8.8 billion if other index providers followed.

MSCI eventually nixed the proposal, but Brown points to what happened next. The firm froze increases in the number of shares it would count for affected companies and deferred new additions while preparing a broader review.

Bitcoin Rule Returns Wearing a Different Hat

Seven months later, Brown writes, MSCI came back with a broader test that no longer singled out bitcoin (BTC) or digital assets by name. Instead, the August proposal centers on whether a company has enough “operating assets.” A company failing the initial 50% screen faces five additional financial tests and, if it isn’t already an index constituent, can be excluded after triggering four of them. Existing constituents receive buffers and generally must fail during two consecutive annual reviews before removal.

Here’s where Brown sees a fundamental problem. His paper says “operating assets” isn’t a standardized balance-sheet category under U.S. GAAP or IFRS, leaving MSCI to classify everything from cash and mineral rights to unfinished construction, intellectual property and strategic holdings before the math can even begin.

Brown also zeroes in on Strategy’s bitcoin accounting. The company reported $22.8 billion in bitcoin-related operating losses during the first half of 2026, compared with $195 million in its other operating expenses. Count those figures as Strategy filed them, Brown argues, and one of MSCI’s flags wouldn’t be triggered. The 23-page paper contends that reaching MSCI’s simulated result, therefore, requires an analytical reclassification that the consultation doesn’t disclose.

The Uranium Twist Breaks the Story Wide Open

Brown’s argument gets considerably stranger once bitcoin leaves the picture. MSCI’s simulated deletions also include Yellow Cake, a company that holds physical uranium. The Bitcoin Policy Institute paper then takes the proposed methodology for a spin across other capital-intensive businesses, illustrating how the same logic might reach companies building satellites or a major U.S. lithium mine.

Under one plausible interpretation examined by Brown, AST Spacemobile could trigger four of MSCI’s flags and potentially be barred as a new index entrant. Lithium Americas presents an even sharper example. The company is building the Thacker Pass lithium project in Nevada, and Brown’s analysis finds it could also trigger four flags.

Lithium Americas reported $3.54 billion in assets in June, including $2.09 billion in mineral properties, plant and equipment. Yet Brown’s paper shows how a restrictive reading of MSCI’s proposal could make a mine still under construction look “non-operating” precisely because it’s expensive to build, hasn’t begun producing revenue and depends heavily on outside financing. The bigger the unfinished project, in other words, the stranger the accounting picture can become.

MSCI is expected to decide on or before Oct. 16, with any adopted changes slated for its November index review around Dec. 1. Brown’s paper starts with bitcoin treasury companies, but its argument ultimately lands somewhere much bigger. When trillions of dollars mechanically follow an index, the definition of what counts as an operating business is anything but academic.

title: Animoca Brands’ Moca Chain Takes Aim at Digital Identity
summary: The Moca Foundation and Moca Network have launched a decentralized blockchain that lets users and AI agents securely share verified credentials across applications. Decoupling Verification from Data Storage Moca Foundation and Moca Network, an Animoca Brands project, have launched a blockchain netwo...
content:
The Moca Foundation and Moca Network have launched a decentralized blockchain that lets users and AI agents securely share verified credentials across applications.

Key Takeaways

  • Moca Foundation and Moca Network launched the Moca Chain mainnet to manage decentralized digital identities.
  • The launch addresses growing privacy risks caused by $100B+ in annual data custody costs and AI agent web traffic.
  • Over 9 partners, including SK Planet and Automobili Lamborghini, plan to integrate Moca Network’s AIR in 2026.

Decoupling Verification from Data Storage

Moca Foundation and Moca Network, an Animoca Brands project, have launched a blockchain network allowing users to carry verified digital credentials across applications without repeatedly sharing their underlying personal information. The network focuses on digital identity and enables organizations to issue verifiable credentials covering information such as identity verification and membership status.

According to Moca Network, users retain custody of those credentials and determine when and where they are shared. The launch comes as businesses increasingly grapple with fragmented digital identity systems that require customers to undergo similar verification procedures across multiple platforms. Moca Network argues that the problem could become more pronounced as artificial intelligence (AI) agents increasingly conduct transactions and interact with online services on behalf of users.

Under Moca Chain’s decentralized verification model, organizations can verify user information and issue tamper-resistant credentials linked to a unified digital identity. The approach reduces the amount of sensitive information companies need to store.

Moca Network is pairing the blockchain with AIR, which provides businesses with a single integration point for onboarding users and AI agents. Companies can use AIR to turn existing customer verification checks into credentials on Moca Chain or accept credentials issued by trusted third-parties.

The company argues that such verification infrastructure will become increasingly important as autonomous agents account for a greater share of online activity.

“Users should not be forced to surrender sensitive personal information redundantly every time they use a new service and platform,” Yat Siu, co-founder and executive chairman of Animoca Brands, said in a statement.

Reducing Redundant Data Requests

Siu said repeated verification requirements are not only cumbersome, but can create barriers that discourage users from moving between competing platforms.

“As more and more AI agents navigate the digital economy on behalf of more and more people, Moca Chain is ideally positioned to provide individuals with sovereign ownership of their credentials, and to give businesses a mechanism that can establish trust without unnecessary data custody,” he said.

Meanwhile, Moca Network revealed that AIR’s ecosystem includes integrations with consumer platforms, fintech companies, loyalty programs, and agentic commerce projects. Partners named by the company include South Korea’s SK Planet, ticketing platform Biletinial, gaming marketplace Oyunfor, Open Campus, soccer platform OneFootball, Automobili Lamborghini, Inveo Kripto, Plume, and blockchain analytics company Nansen.

Kenneth Shek, CEO of Moca Network, described Moca Chain as infrastructure intended to make identity information available and changes to identity credentials auditable.

“Scalable data sharing is necessary for AI agents to act on behalf of humans; however, the trust framework for delegation and authority is lacking,” Shek said.

He added that AIR is designed to allow AI agents to perform tasks while users retain control over their personal data and permissions.

title: Coinbase-Backed Base Gives Users More Control With Cobalt Upgrade
summary: Base has launched Cobalt, its third major network upgrade, adding new transaction controls for traders and expanding tools for companies issuing tokens on the Coinbase-incubated Ethereum Layer 2 network. Base Debuts Transaction Controls The upgrade is now live on Base mainnet and centers on two area...
content:
Base has launched Cobalt, its third major network upgrade, adding new transaction controls for traders and expanding tools for companies issuing tokens on the Coinbase-incubated Ethereum Layer 2 network.

Key Takeaways

  • Base’s Cobalt upgrade adds “Validity Transactions,” allowing users to set conditions and expiration times for when transactions can be executed.
  • The upgrade expands Base’s B20 token standard with compliance controls, scheduled token adjustments, and administrative transfer tools.
  • Base said Cobalt is part of a broader roadmap that includes faster block times, smart accounts, and additional EVM improvements.

Base Debuts Transaction Controls

The upgrade is now live on Base mainnet and centers on two areas: a new feature called “Validity Transactions” and enhancements to Base’s B20 token standard, according to a blog post published by Base.

Validity Transactions are designed to let users submit transactions that only become eligible for inclusion when preset conditions are met. A trader, for example, could sign and submit a swap that remains dormant until an asset reaches a particular price, while also setting a deadline after which the transaction expires.

Base said the feature could reduce the need for traders to continuously monitor markets and resubmit transactions. Submissions can also remain private until they are included onchain, potentially offering additional flexibility for sophisticated trading strategies. Base emphasized that users themselves set the conditions and sign the transactions.

Cobalt also introduces several updates to B20, Base’s native token standard aimed at asset issuers. One addition, called Composite Policies, lets issuers combine requirements such as know-your-customer allowlists, accreditation rules, and sanctions blocklists using logical conditions. That could allow tokenized financial products to rely on multiple compliance providers without maintaining duplicate lists.

Another feature enables issuers to schedule changes to a token’s display multiplier, which Base said could support corporate actions such as stock splits without changing underlying balances. Cobalt also introduces “seizeWithMemo,” a function that allows authorized administrators of supported tokens to reassign balances while attaching an onchain explanation of the transfer.

The changes reflect Base’s broader push to position its network as infrastructure not only for crypto trading and payments, but also for issuing and managing tokenized assets.

Base said additional upgrades are planned in the coming months, including reducing block times from two seconds to 200 milliseconds, introducing protocol-level smart account functionality, and implementing further Ethereum Virtual Machine improvements. Developers cautioned that those plans remain subject to change.

Prominent crypto exchange Coinbase debuted the Base network in 2023, building upon the Optimism tech stack used by some other Ethereum Layer 2 scaling networks. In February 2026, however, the company said that it would transition the network to its own, bespoke technology, with the Cobalt upgrade adding further refinement to the current incarnation of Base. Coinbase said last year that it is considering launching a native token for Base.

title: Standard Chartered sees Ethena’s USDe reaching $40B, ENA hitting $2
summary: The bank also expects Ethena’s ENA token to rise roughly sevenfold to $2 by the end of 2028 as USDe scales and token buybacks increase.
content:
British multinational bank Standard Chartered expects Ethena’s USDe stablecoin supply to grow eightfold to $40 billion by the end of 2028 as the protocol expands its sources of yield beyond crypto markets.

In a Wednesday research report shared with Cointelegraph, the bank initiated coverage of Ethena’s ENA token with a year-end 2028 price target of $2, roughly seven times the $0.28 price cited in the report. Standard Chartered also expects USDe to slightly outpace overall stablecoin market growth over the period.

Its forecasts imply ENA would also outperform Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH) through 2028. Standard Chartered sees BTC reaching $300,000 and ETH $18,000 by the end of the period.

Standard Chartered’s year-end digital asset price forecasts through 2028. Source: Standard Chartered Research

Standard Chartered said declining returns from USDe’s traditional crypto basis trade, which involves holding spot crypto while shorting perpetual futures, have pushed Ethena to expand into DeFi and institutional lending, real-world assets and basis trades tied to equities and commodities. Those sources currently generate a blended yield of 5.2%, giving USDe more room to scale.

The bank forecasts the broader market for tokenized assets will grow from about $350 billion today to $4 trillion by the end of 2028, expanding the pool of assets Ethena could use to generate yield.

Related: Ethena launches USDe payments app, offers 6% rewards

USDe growth could fuel ENA buybacks

The link between USDe growth and ENA buybacks is central to Standard Chartered’s valuation case for the token. A fee switch approved by Ethena governance in early September directs 95% of net revenue from its business lines toward ENA buybacks once USDe reaches specified supply milestones.

At $25 billion in USDe supply, Ethena estimates the mechanism could generate $375 million in annual ENA buybacks, assuming a 6% gross protocol yield and a 25% net revenue take rate.

ENA buyback volumes at different USDe supply levels. Source: Ethena

Standard Chartered estimates that if USDe reaches its $40 billion forecast and ENA’s price remains unchanged, annual buybacks could amount to roughly 23% of ENA’s circulating market capitalization. The bank said such a rate would likely be unsustainable, so it expects ENA’s price to rise until buybacks settle at a lower percentage of its market value.

The bank used Uniswap as a comparison, noting that UNI’s annualized buyback rate has stabilized at around 3% to 4% as its token price increased.

ENA was trading at about $0.27 on Wednesday, up roughly 28% over the past week and 77% over the past month, according to CoinGecko data. The token has a market capitalization of about $2.65 billion.

title: Bitcoin Price Holds $83K as Bitfinex Says Leverage Has Cleared
summary: Bitcoin calls represent 60.88% of options open interest, while Deribit’s October max-pain level sits near $76,000, below bitcoin’s current $83,719 spot price. Futures exposure totals approximately $53 billion, led by Binance and CME. The market data on Wednesday shows concentrated October call posit...
content:
Bitcoin calls represent 60.88% of options open interest, while Deribit’s October max-pain level sits near $76,000, below bitcoin’s current $83,719 spot price. Futures exposure totals approximately $53 billion, led by Binance and CME. The market data on Wednesday shows concentrated October call positions, mixed exchange activity, and a substantially smaller CME options book than in late 2025, with expiry mechanics complicating directional interpretations.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance holds $11.01 billion in bitcoin futures open interest, representing 20.77% of the market.
  • Deribit’s Oct. 30 $95,000 call leads displayed options positions with 23,350.8 BTC in open interest.
  • CME options data shows a smaller book than late 2025, with calls outweighing puts in the latest tape.

Bitcoin options carry a split personality into October, with calls accounting for 60.88% of outstanding positions, according to Coinglass stats. October has traditionally treated bitcoin well, earning the month the “Uptober” moniker among crypto proponents. Yet while most Octobers since 2013 have finished in the green, the pattern broke in 2025 when bitcoin failed to deliver a gain despite hitting a new high early in the month.

At the same time, September, historically one of bitcoin’s more punishing months over the past 14 years, flipped the script this year with a 7% gain. Could this mean the infamous “Uptober” may fail to materialize? Meanwhile, Deribit’s Oct. 30 max-pain level sits near $76,000, roughly $8,000 below bitcoin’s $84,144 price at 2 p.m. Eastern on Sept. 30, 2026.

The apparent contradiction puts upside exposure beside a much lower options payout reference point, while roughly $53 billion in futures open interest adds another layer of exposure to a market whose biggest venues aren’t moving in lockstep.

Bitcoin Futures Show Divided Exchange Activity

Futures figures on Wednesday show approximately $53 billion total from individual exchanges. Binance currently holds $11.01 billion, or 20.77% of the tally, against CME’s $8.46 billion and 15.96% sahre. Together, they represent nearly $37 of every $100 in outstanding futures exposure. Open interest measures outstanding contracts, not cash deposited or money newly entering bitcoin.

The next sizable books include Bybit at $5.22 billion, MEXC at $5.05 billion, and Gate at $4.27 billion. The decentralized perps exchange Hyperliquid carries $3.04 billion, ahead of OKX’s $2.94 billion. Historical futures data ends near $53 billion today, well below its visible peak above $90 billion last year. That’s a smaller book, though dollar totals also move with bitcoin’s price.

Over 24 hours, Binance’s open interest rose 2.10% and CME’s gained 1.41%, while Bybit lost 2.54% and OKX shed 1.89%. BingX posted a 37.34% increase to $918.61 million. Zoom into four hours, however, and Binance, CME, Bybit, and OKX all contracted. The shorter window throws cold water on any claim of uniform expansion.

Bitfinex Analysts See Room for Gains as Speculative Froth Clears

In a note shared with Bitcoin.com News on Wednesday afternoon, Bitfinex analysts explained that a lot of the borrowed money and aggressive betting has left the bitcoin market.

“Aggregated futures open interest (OI) is at its lowest since March, implied volatility (IV) sits close to a one-year low, and Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) inflows have slowed to roughly match the pace of new bitcoin issuance,” Bitfinex analysts wrote. “With leverage substantially reduced, the next sustained move will need to be led by the spot market.”

Traders are using less leverage, and futures are offering less incentive to make aggressive bets on bitcoin’s price. Bitfinex said that has sometimes been a healthy setup for bitcoin’s price.

“This combination of contracting OI in response to diminished futures premiums has historically supported price action,” the market strategists explained. “Since 2022, elevated futures settlement ratios paired with compressed carry have preceded a median 30-day gain of 8.9 percent. If current basis rates persist and OI remains flat, the historical patterns suggest that bitcoin could continue to appreciate.”

The Bitfinex analyst team added:

“We expect the current band to decide the next move. While the $82,500 to $84,000 cost basis keeps thickening, buyers are absorbing the coins that overhead holders sell, and each day of that dynamic reduces the supply waiting at breakeven. A reclaim of $85,000 would return the 760,000 BTC held between $84,000 and $85,000 to profit and lift supply in profit back above 75%. At that point, those holders stop being sellers.”

Calls Dominate Bitcoin Options Positions

Options open interest stands around $36 billion this afternoon, after a recent spike above $50 billion before the last big expiry. The call-versus-put panel lists 262,739.4 BTC in calls and 168,854.8 BTC in puts, a put-to-call ratio near 0.64. Calls represent roughly three-fifths of outstanding exposure, but their numerical advantage doesn’t indicate whether traders bought or sold them.

Daily options volume is more evenly divided: 55.08% calls against 44.92% puts, with 34,514.02 BTC and 28,151.67 BTC traded, respectively. Calls provide upside rights; puts provide downside rights. Either can feature in hedges or multileg strategies. A call-heavy tally, by itself, doesn’t establish a marketwide bullish wager. The fine print earns its keep.

Deribit’s Oct. 30 $95,000 call tops the displayed contract rankings on Wednesday with 23,350.8 BTC of open interest. The $90,000 and $100,000 calls for that expiry follow with 18,089.4 BTC and 12,956.7 BTC. Those three strikes total 54,396.9 BTC. Meanwhile, the Oct. 1 $84,000 put ranks second in daily volume, showing activity close to the supplied spot price.

CME Options Shrink Across Expirations

Cryptoquant’s CME expiry metrics show a much smaller outstanding book at September’s end than during late 2025, when plotted totals exceeded 70,000. Recent totals fall sharply from roughly 11,000 to around 6,000 as the nearest bucket drops out. CME’s separate dollar-denominated options stats also end far below late-2025 levels. Calls visually outweigh puts in the latest action, reversing the put-heavy composition visible through much of the intervening period.

Max Pain Sits Below Spot Price

For Oct. 30, the latest max-pain levels are approximately $76,000 on Deribit, $79,000 on Binance, and $80,000 on OKX. Deribit’s October and December expiries each carry roughly $10 billion in notional value. Max pain is the price at which option holders would collect the least at expiration, not a forecast of where bitcoin will land.

December’s reference levels also remain below bitcoin’s price, sitting near $75,000 on Deribit and OKX and around $80,000 on Binance. October’s largest listed call positions, meanwhile, stretch from $90,000 to $100,000, even as the underlying payout math points considerably lower. Both sets of numbers share the same options board, reflecting a market where traders are positioned across a wide range of possible outcomes.

title: UK Brings Crypto Under Full FCA Oversight for the First Time
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

UK Brings Crypto Under Full FCA Oversight for the First Time
The British regulator has started accepting applications from crypto companies ahead of a new regime taking effect next year.
This post UK Brings Crypto Under Full FCA Oversight for the First Time first appeared on Bitcoi...
content:
The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority has opened applications for crypto firms to become authorized, bringing the sector under full regulation for the first time.

In a Wednesday announcement, the watchdog said companies can apply so that the crypto industry has “clarity and legitimacy.”

The UK is in the process of drafting a sweeping new crypto bill. The FCA finalized its regulatory framework for cryptoassets in June, and the regime is due to take effect in October 2027.  

“The UK’s new crypto regime will give consumers greater protections and firms a clear framework to operate in. Firms can now apply for authorisation and start preparing for regulation,” Dominic Cashman, director of authorisation at the FCA, said in a statement. 

The statement added that firms will have to demonstrate that they meet requirements covering consumer protection, customer-asset safeguarding, market integrity and financial resilience.

Britain is pushing ahead with digital asset legislation since last year recognizing bitcoin and other digital assets as property. The reform came from a 2023 recommendation by the Law Commission, which argued that digital assets did not fit neatly into existing legal categories.

Despite the FCA’s announcement, the UK currently is trailing behind Brussels and Washington with digital asset regulation. 

The EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation has applied to service providers since 30 December 2024. 

And the U.S. under President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act into law in July 2025, establishing a federal framework for dollar-backed tokens.

Despite lawmakers blocking landmark legislation the Clarity Act last month, U.S. regulators like the Securities and Exchange Commission have pushed ahead with rulemaking regardless. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Bitcoin Surges 40% in Its Best Quarter Since Late 2024
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Surges 40% in Its Best Quarter Since Late 2024
The price of bitcoin has surged — mostly since the Treasury announced its debt buyback program — putting it on course for one of its best quarters ever. 
This post Bitcoin Surges 40% in Its Best Quarter Since Late 2024 first ap...
content:
Bitcoin is having one of its best quarters ever — another indication that the biggest cryptocurrency is in a bull market. 

As noted by the The Kobeissi Letter this week, the price of bitcoin is now up close to 30% since August 19, when the U.S. Treasury announced it planned to more than double the size of its government debt repurchases.

Over the past quarter, the bitcoin price has surged by 40% — its best quarterly performance since Q4 2024. 

Bitcoin’s price recently stood at nearly $83,698, unmoved over a 24-hour period but up 6% over a 30-day period. 

The coin has benefited from news that the Treasury would try to lower bond yields — which have soared to highs not seen since the 2000s. 

Bitcoin has done well with lower long-term yields because it reduces the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like bitcoin and gold, and generally supports risk-on sentiment. 

But despite the Treasury stepping in to try and tame the bond market, yields have continued to stay high. 

Bitcoin investors don’t seem that bothered. The asset is still doing well as the dollar continues to slip. The so-called debasement trade — where investors throw money at an asset to hedge against a currency losing its value — is hot again after total U.S. debt topped $40 trillion for the first time in July.  

The price of Bitcoin had been battered since notching a new all-time high of $126,080 in October, dropping by over 50%. Still, it has experienced the shallowest bear market — so far — in its history. 

CryptoQuant said in a report last week that bitcoin was back in a bull market after crossing above its 365-day moving average — the “definitive technical signal” that has marked the start of Bitcoin’s bull markets in past cycles.

The coin has shrugged off the Federal Reserve raising interest rates and lawmakers blockage of landmark crypto legislation, the Clarity Act. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Does America.gov Know Bitcoin Policy as Well as ChatGPT and Claude? We Asked
summary: The newly launched U.S. government AI chatbot America.gov can also help bitcoin and crypto users with answers to their questions. However, those responses can still be outdated, misleading, or self-censored. Bitcoin.com News compared answers from America.gov, Claude, and ChatGPT to 12 crypto policy ...
content:
The newly launched U.S. government AI chatbot America.gov can also help bitcoin and crypto users with answers to their questions. However, those responses can still be outdated, misleading, or self-censored. Bitcoin.com News compared answers from America.gov, Claude, and ChatGPT to 12 crypto policy questions.

Key Takeaways

  • America.gov provided useful official sources but missed some recent crypto legislation.
  • Claude and ChatGPT offered more context on recent crypto regulatory developments.
  • America.gov often hedged its answers and included “not advice” caveats.

The new government website, designed to be a “unified digital front door” to the federal government, launched on Sept. 29. “You’ll save hours and hours, many hours, hundreds of hours perhaps, a year, depending on how much of that type of information you need,” President Donald Trump said during the launch event on Tuesday.

Gemini and Grok Behind America.gov

Google confirmed that the company behind the popular Gemini AI model is a technology partner on the project. U.S. Chief Design Officer Joe Gebbia added that Grok from Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI was also used in developing the platform.

Bitcoin.com News tested the platform, which, according to the government, pulls information and updates from around 29,000 government websites.

We asked 12 questions related to the federal government’s bitcoin and crypto policies, tax reporting, crypto asset usage, investor protection, and the Trump family’s crypto businesses. With Claude, Bitcoin.com News used the Sonnet 5.5 model at high effort, while ChatGPT was tested using the standard free version.

America.gov Misses What Is Happening in America

In general, America.gov was strong on tax forms, scam reporting, and safety warnings. However, unlike Claude and ChatGPT, it missed recent legislative developments relevant to the questions. It also presented outdated information about the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’s guidance on digital assets.

In either case, the platform, similarly to Claude, constantly hedged, adding a “not advice” line to its answers while also saying what it could not do in nine out of 12 questions. ChatGPT added none of these caveats.

Let’s look at those differences in more detail. For space and simplicity, Bitcoin.com News will provide America.gov’s answers while adding a comment on how Claude and ChatGPT performed in each case.

1. What is the status of the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill?

ChatGPT was the clearest here, while Claude was the most detailed. America.gov was out of date because it missed the fact that, on Sept. 16, a House committee advanced legislation that would codify the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve. Both other chatbots mentioned this vote. Meanwhile, the structure-loving ChatGPT summed it up most succinctly: “Strategic Bitcoin Reserve = already established policy. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve in federal statute = not yet law.”

2. How does the government protect my bitcoin and crypto investments?

All three were correct in essence: The protection is very limited. Claude provided the most current information, mentioning the GENIUS and CLARITY acts. Meanwhile, America.gov, while noting that crypto asset accounts are not backed by the government and listing various regulators’ positions, also warned that only criminals will ask for your private keys and seed phrases.

3. How to know whether my crypto is a security?

America.gov sends users to the SEC’s withdrawn guidance, while ChatGPT was the most detailed in naming crypto assets that are not securities. It also mentioned the SEC’s September FAQs as “staff guidance, not law or binding Commission rules.” Meanwhile, Claude said that “there’s no official list you can look up,” despite regulatory agencies mentioning specific tokens. “I cannot review your wallet or name a coin’s status,” America.gov wrote.

4. How do I report crypto on my federal tax return?

America.gov was the most useful of the bunch here, providing the most complete checklist. Meanwhile, only ChatGPT noted that paying a network fee in a crypto asset can itself be a small taxable disposal.

5. Is buying a coffee with bitcoin taxable?

Simple question, simple answer, and all three chatbots were correct, while the fight for the de minimis tax exemption is ongoing. Claude went a bit further into detail, adding that bitcoin payments via the Lightning Network are taxable too.

6. Can my crypto count toward a mortgage application?

America.gov was the most precise here on the current rule, while Claude mentioned how a person can use BTC or USDC as collateral without selling them. “You shouldn’t assume that $200,000 of BTC sitting in self-custody will be treated like $200,000 in a checking account,” ChatGPT concluded.

7. Are stablecoins FDIC-insured?

All three chatbots answered correctly—no, stablecoins are not Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation-insured. However, while America.gov didn’t mention the GENIUS Act elsewhere, where it was also relevant, it mentioned it in this answer. Meanwhile, ChatGPT’s answer seemed to be the least valuable in terms of detail.

8. What did the CLARITY Act change for crypto investors?

This is somewhat of a trick question, as the CLARITY Act failed an important vote in the Senate on Sept. 16. This recent detail was caught by both ChatGPT and Claude. However, in essence, America.gov wasn’t wrong either, writing that it can’t confirm from its sources that the act is law. America.gov described in the most detail what the bill would change if passed.

9. Can I hold bitcoin in my 401(k)?

All three confirmed that there is no federal right to hold bitcoin in a 401(k) and that this depends on your plan. Meanwhile, both Claude and ChatGPT offered more practical ways to do it, for example, via a bitcoin ETF. America.gov mentioned brokerage windows.

10. My crypto exchange went bankrupt. Is my money protected?

Here, America.gov was also correct, while Claude and ChatGPT provided more practical details, explaining that different situations might affect fund recovery differently.

11. How do I report a crypto scam, and can I get my money back?

All three provided similarly actionable steps, relevant links, and advice. For example, America.gov urged users to stop sending money and not tell the scammer that they had been reported. The government chatbot was also the best at providing relevant links where crypto crimes can be reported. Meanwhile, Claude and ChatGPT offered the most hope that the funds might sometimes be recovered.

12. What are the ethical and legal implications of Trump and his family co-owning World Liberty Financial?

America.gov refused to answer because it doesn’t “provide political commentary or legal advice.” Meanwhile, the other two chatbots offered more insights and details. “Whether it should be barred is a question for Congress and voters, and I’ll leave that judgment to you,” Claude concluded, while ChatGPT wrote that “potential conflict of interest” and “illegal conflict of interest” are not interchangeable conclusions in the case of a sitting U.S. president.

Another Chatbot You Need to Verify

So what do all these answers tell us about the government chatbot launched on Sept. 29?

For now, it appears to be most helpful for finding the official form, hotline, or rule when it comes to crypto assets. Meanwhile, if you need more context and the latest developments, other chatbots might serve you better, as America.gov is designed to use government sources only.

“AI can make mistakes, so check the sources included with each answer before making an important decision,” the platform’s own FAQ section warns.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, a Coinbase-backed advocacy group endorsed candidates in key congressional races ahead of the US midterms, the United Kingdom opened applications for crypto firms seeking authorization under its new regulatory regime and Crypto.com’s personal AI agent platform remains in “stealth mode” nearly eight months after its Super Bowl debut.

Stand With Crypto backs congressional candidates ahead of midterms

Stand With Crypto has endorsed candidates in several key Senate and House races as the crypto industry steps up its involvement ahead of the US November midterm elections.

The Coinbase-backed advocacy group is supporting Republican Sen. Jon Husted in Ohio, Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson in Iowa and Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas in New Hampshire. It also endorsed House candidates from both parties, including Democrat Shomari Figures in Alabama and Republican Mariannette Miller-Meeks in Iowa.

The endorsements come two weeks after the Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act, which would establish a federal regulatory framework for crypto markets. Stand With Crypto has since updated its candidate scorecard to reflect lawmakers’ votes on the bill and plans to increase advertising in six House races.

Crypto money is already flowing into several races. Fairshake, the industry-backed super PAC funded largely by Coinbase, Ripple and Andreessen Horowitz, has committed $30 million to support Husted against Democrat Sherrod Brown in Ohio.

FCA opens crypto authorization window ahead of 2027 UK regime

The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) opened applications Wednesday for crypto businesses seeking authorization under a regulatory regime due to take effect on Oct. 25, 2027.

Companies intending to continue operating in the UK should apply by the end of February 2027. The FCA expects to decide applications submitted during that window before the regime takes effect.

The framework expands the FCA’s oversight beyond anti-money laundering and financial promotion requirements. The regulator finalized its rules in June, including requirements covering stablecoin issuance, crypto trading platforms and market abuse.

“The UK’s new crypto regime will give consumers greater protections and firms a clear framework to operate in,” said Dominic Cashman, the FCA’s director of authorization.

Emma Banymandhub, CEO of payments industry trade body The Payments Association, welcomed the opening but urged businesses already registered under money laundering regulations (MLRs) to treat it as a fresh authorization process.

“MLR registration will not carry over, and firms should be realistic about the standards they will need to meet,” she said in comments shared with Cointelegraph.

Crypto.com AI agent still in ‘stealth mode’ nearly 8 months after Super Bowl debut

Crypto.com says its personal AI agent venture, pitched to perform a broad set of tasks from trading stocks to updating online dating profiles, is still under construction, months after a Super Bowl debut that got so much attention it crashed the website.

Ai.com, a business line of Crypto.com, promoted the launch of its AI platform in a $15 million ad during the fourth quarter of the Super Bowl in February. The website crashed within minutes as curious users flocked to reserve a handle for their own personal AI agent. 

However, nearly eight months later, the website continues to display a message that AI agent generation is queued due to high demand.

Speaking to Cointelegraph, a spokesperson for Crypto.com confirmed the AI agent platform is still being worked on. “ai.com continues building in stealth mode; we are happy to provide more details when we fully launch to the public,” they said. 

The prolonged wait comes as rival exchanges have already begun offering AI assistants focused on narrower tasks, such as trading and portfolio management. 

Cointelegraph is committed to independent, transparent journalism. This news article is produced in accordance with Cointelegraph’s Editorial Policy and aims to provide accurate and timely information. Readers are encouraged to verify information independently.

title: OpenAI Launches Dots AI Agent Across 4,000+ Apps After GPT-6 Astra Delay
summary: OpenAI has launched Dots, a new class of always-on AI agents designed to work independently on users’ goals across more than 4,000 connected applications.
content:
Skip to content

OpenAI has launched Dots, a new class of always-on AI agents designed to work independently on users’ goals across more than 4,000 connected applications.

The launch came one day after OpenAI confirmed it had shelved the planned release of GPT-6.1 Astra following internal testing that identified safety and alignment problems.

OpenAI unveiled Dots during its DevDay event in San Francisco on September 29. The company describes them as “remarkably capable, always-on agents” that can learn a user’s preferences, operate through their own cloud computer and browser, and continue working toward assigned goals without requiring constant prompts.

The technology is aimed at moving AI agents beyond one-off responses toward persistent digital assistance. Dots can handle tasks ranging from research and data analysis to software development and workplace coordination. They can also remain accessible through ChatGPT, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.

What are OpenAI’s new Dots?

OpenAI’s Dots are persistent AI agents that can take responsibility for multi-step tasks rather than simply responding to individual prompts. Users can assign a goal and allow the agent to determine the steps required to make progress.

OpenAI introduced “dots,” always-on AI agents powered by GPT-6 Astra that automate tasks across more than 4,000 apps. Source: @OpenAI via X

Each Dot has its own cloud computer, browser, and access to connected applications. The company says its plugin ecosystem allows Dots to connect to more than 4,000 apps. The company says agents can continue working on multiple projects while users add new tasks or ideas.

The system is powered by GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI’s model designed for demanding reasoning, coding, research, computer use, and other complex work. The company’s documentation describes Astra as its most capable model for demanding workloads, with support for large context windows and multiple reasoning levels.

OpenAI is also emphasizing personalization. Dots can learn from user feedback and gradually adapt to preferences, working standards, and goals. The company says users can communicate with their agents through ChatGPT, Slack, or Teams, as well as through voice.

The company provided several examples of how the system could be used. A Dot could monitor customer feedback, identify recurring software issues, prepare fixes, and create pull requests for a developer to review. In another example, it could update research as new evidence becomes available or revise sales materials when customer requirements change.

An OpenAI engineer demonstrated Dots handling tasks that would typically require an entire team, highlighting its potential to automate workplace workflows. Source: Anatoli Kopadze via X

OpenAI also demonstrated the concept through animated Dot characters during its launch presentation. The playful presentation contrasts with the underlying system, which is intended for tasks that can involve multiple applications and extended periods of autonomous work.

The company said Dots are initially rolling out across ChatGPT Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise plans in eligible markets, with availability expanding over time. They also said the first primary Dot is included without an additional charge.

Control remains a central part of the product. Users can inspect a Dot’s cloud computer and review its work. OpenAI has also outlined access permissions, action reviews, approvals, and other safeguards intended to limit what an agent can do without user authorization.

OpenAI said it eventually expects multiple Dots to work together. It is also previewing specialist Dots designed for organizations, with dedicated identities, access-management features, and deeper integrations with business systems.

Why is OpenAI launching Dots now?

The timing of the Dots launch is notable because it followed OpenAI’s decision to halt the planned release of GPT-6.1 Astra. Reuters reported that the model, which had been expected in October, was shelved after internal testing found that it did not meet the company’s safety and alignment standards.

According to Reuters, internal testing found instances in which GPT-6.1 Astra showed higher levels of deceptive behavior than its predecessor and did not always accurately communicate the actions it had taken. Saachi Jain, OpenAI’s head of safety systems, said the model had improved in areas such as reducing “model laziness” but had fallen short on staying within scope and authorization.

OpenAI announced “dots,” always-on AI agents powered by GPT-6 Astra that function as persistent personal assistants. Source: @OpenAI via X

Jain said OpenAI maintains an “extremely high bar” for safety and alignment before releasing models to users. The company’s decision to delay GPT-6.1 Astra therefore placed additional attention on how the copmany intends to manage the risks associated with increasingly autonomous systems.

Dots introduce a related challenge because they are designed to take actions rather than only generate information. An agent with access to a browser, cloud computer, and thousands of applications can potentially carry out much longer sequences of tasks with less direct supervision.

OpenAI says its Dots system is built around user controls and approval mechanisms. The company allows users to inspect an agent’s work and define what applications and actions it can access. For some tasks, the Dot can prepare work for approval instead of completing the final action independently.

The launch also follows broader scrutiny of autonomous AI systems. Reuters has reported on incidents involving AI systems interacting with external websites and other connected environments, including an OpenAI system that accessed an Australian government health portal. The company has also been reviewing model behavior involving public government websites.

Those incidents have made authorization, monitoring, and containment increasingly important as AI agents gain access to real-world tools. The issue is not limited to OpenAI. Other AI developers are also working on systems that can execute multi-step tasks with limited human intervention.

OpenAI is consequently positioning Dots not simply as another chatbot feature but as an AI agent platform that can remain active between conversations. The company’s stated goal is for these systems to take on ongoing responsibilities while leaving users responsible for important decisions and approvals.

The launch also places OpenAI in a rapidly developing agentic AI market. Companies across the technology sector are building systems that can interact with software, communicate with people, and complete extended workflows rather than stopping after generating a single response.

For OpenAI, Dots provides a direct way to put the capabilities of GPT-6 Astra into persistent workflows. At the same time, the recent GPT-6.1 Astra delay illustrates why the company’s approach to permissions, monitoring, and human oversight will remain an important part of the rollout as autonomous AI agents become more capable.

title: Crypto advocacy group announces picks for US Congress as midterms loom
summary: The organization’s endorsements in the House and Senate came as many polls showed Democrats favored to regain control of both chambers in 2027.
content:
Update (Sept. 30, 10:55 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a response from Stand With Crypto.

Stand With Crypto, the industry-aligned organization Coinbase launched in 2023 to promote what it called “clear, common-sense regulations for the crypto industry,” has announced several picks for the next session of the US Congress.

On Wednesday, Bloomberg first reported that Stand With Crypto said it would be supporting candidates running for Senate seats in 2026, including Republican Jon Husted in Ohio, Republican Ashley Hinson in Iowa and Democrat Chris Pappas in New Hampshire. Husted is defending his Senate seat against Democrat Sherrod Brown, who lost to Republican Bernie Moreno in 2024 after outside groups spent more than $300 million in Ohio.

In addition to the Senate seats, the advocacy organization said it had endorsed several House of Representatives candidates, including Republican Mariannette Miller-Meeks in Iowa and Democrat Shomari Figures in Alabama. The group’s picks come as many polls show Democrats favored to regain control of the House and Senate in 2027.

A shakeup in majority control of either chamber of Congress could change how lawmakers address bills like the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act. The crypto market structure bill failed to get enough votes in the Republican-controlled Senate earlier this month for a crucial cloture motion after passing the House with bipartisan support in 2025. 

Related: Illinois draft crypto tax rules detail DeFi, stablecoin treatment

Stand With Crypto endorsed 32 House candidates in August whom it called “proven digital asset policy champions,” citing the potential to sway voters in key races.

How the vote on a crypto bill could impact US elections

After the failed CLARITY vote on Sept. 15, Stand With Crypto warned of “consequences” for lawmakers who did not support the bill.

With just 34 days until the midterm elections, some candidates have already been flooded with money from the crypto industry filtered through political action committees (PACs) and direct donations to campaigns. The Fairshake PAC, a group largely backed by contributions from Coinbase, Ripple Labs and Andreessen Horowitz, pledged to initially spend $30 million supporting Husted over Brown in Ohio and spent $82 million on candidates across the country as of June.

Speaking to Cointelegraph on the spending in the Senate run between Husted and Brown, Stand With Crypto Executive Director Mason Lynaugh said that there “isn’t any evidence that crypto industry organizations are able to buy any assurances of who will win a race.“ He said that Husted was a “proven pro-crypto lawmaker“ and the organization’s endorsement was due to the Ohio lawmaker’s vote in favor of the CLARITY Act, the industry’s “top policy priority.“

“[W]hen his opponent [Brown] was last in the Senate, he was a leading anti-crypto voice from a very influential position on the Senate Banking Committee,“ said Lynaugh. “Actions speak louder than words. While former Senator Brown’s recent remarks about crypto’s role in the national economy are encouraging, it’s track record that matters the most in our endorsement process.“

title: Base completes Cobalt upgrade, adds new tools for tokenized assets
summary: Base’s Cobalt lets traders set transaction conditions while giving issuers tools for compliance checks, stock splits and forced token transfers.
content:
Base activated its Cobalt upgrade Wednesday, adding conditional transactions and new issuer controls for tokenized assets as the Ethereum layer-2 network deepens its push into onchain finance. 

Cobalt, Base’s third major upgrade, expands its B20 token standard by allowing issuers to apply several compliance checks to the same asset. For example, an issuer could require recipients to pass identity checks, qualify as accredited investors and not appear on a sanctions list.

Issuers can also schedule adjustments for corporate actions such as stock splits. The update changes the number of shares displayed in wallets and apps without minting or burning tokens or altering the underlying balance.

It also allows issuers to give authorized administrators the power to move tokens from a holder’s wallet without the holder’s approval and attach a public note to the transfer. Base said issuers decide whether to enable the feature and who can use it. Base itself cannot initiate such transfers.

The changes give issuers additional compliance and administrative tools needed to bring traditional financial products onchain.

Cobalt also introduces Validity Transactions, which allow users to submit transactions that become eligible for inclusion only when specified onchain conditions are met, giving traders more control over transaction timing.

A trader could submit a swap that becomes eligible only if an asset reaches a specified price before a set block deadline. Base would hold the transaction and evaluate the conditions against the chain’s state as each block is built. Base said transactions submitted through the system can remain private until they are included in a block.

Base sharpens focus on tokenized finance

The Cobalt upgrade builds on Base’s recent push into tokenized finance. On July 8, Base activated B20 as a native token standard for stablecoins, tokenized real-world assets and other fungible tokens, allowing issuers to create assets without building custom token contracts.

On July 16, Base creator Jesse Pollak said the network had made a “wrong bet” by focusing on creator, content and messaging apps and had fallen behind in areas including prediction markets and perpetual futures. 

Related: Coinbase, Apex Group tokenize Bitcoin Yield Fund on Base

Pollak said financial applications, including trading and payments, would become a greater focus as Base sought to develop into a blockchain for global finance. 

The standard has since gained a prominent use case. On Aug. 25, Coinbase launched tokenized US stocks on Base, issuing B20 tokens representing shares in Apple, Nvidia, Meta and Alphabet.

Base said it plans over the coming months to reduce block times from two seconds to 200 milliseconds, introduce protocol-level support for sponsored transaction fees and bundled transactions and adopt some of the technical changes planned for Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade.

title: Bitcoin Is More Than Just an Asset, Says TD Cowen
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Is More Than Just an Asset, Says TD Cowen
TD Cowen says institutions are talking more about how bitcoin can be used to support capital markets. 
This post Bitcoin Is More Than Just an Asset, Says TD Cowen first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo.
content:
Investment bank TD Cowen has said that Bitcoin is more than an asset — and will be increasingly used as financial infrastructure to underpin institutional products.

Writing in a Tuesday note, TD Cowen said that after attending a BitcoinTreasuries Conference this week in New York, it noticed institutions were more than interested in just accumulating the leading cryptocurrency. 

The comments come as major banks around the world delve deeper into the technology that underpins Bitcoin, with firms offering — and using — crypto products for customers and to streamline their own services. 

“Bitcoin increasingly appears to be moving beyond its role as an investable asset and toward a broader role as financial infrastructure capable of supporting new capital-markets activity,” the report read. 

“In our view, the most interesting conversations were not necessarily about bitcoin itself, but about the ecosystem being built around it,” the report continued. 

It added that Bitcoin could be used in its next phase by “supporting capital markets infrastructure.” 

Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin treasury Strategy has long argued that the leading cryptocurrency will underpin other products in the financial sector. The company, which is the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, currently offers preferred stocks which pay investors dividends. 

TD Cowen said that bitcoin custody was becoming more institutional as “larger pools of capital enter the ecosystem.” 

U.S. and European banks have spoken about or started offering bitcoin custody services in recent years. 

BNY Mellon in 2022 became the first major U.S. bank to offer digital asset custody services. And this month, German multinational Deutsche Bank said it would debut a bitcoin custody service for European corporate and institutional clients later in 2026. 

“We believe these developments suggest that bitcoin is continuing to evolve from a standalone asset into a broader financial ecosystem capable of supporting increasingly sophisticated institutional participation,” TD Cowen added.

TD Cowen is a division of multinational TD Securities. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Bloomberg brings onchain stablecoin data to its Terminal
summary: Bloomberg’s Allium-powered dashboard gives Terminal users hourly data on stablecoin supply, issuance, transfers and activity across blockchain networks.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedSep 30, 2026

Bloomberg’s Allium-powered dashboard gives Terminal users hourly data on stablecoin supply, issuance, transfers and activity across blockchain networks.

Bloomberg has launched a stablecoin dashboard on its Terminal, giving financial professionals access to onchain data tracking stablecoin supply, issuance and transaction activity.

The dashboard, powered by blockchain data platform Allium, covers stablecoins with more than $100 million in circulation, representing over 98% of the market, according to a Wednesday announcement from Bloomberg.

Users can compare stablecoins by supply, mints, burns, transfer volume and velocity, and break down activity by blockchain network and peg type, including fiat currencies and commodities.

The dashboard is available to all Bloomberg Terminal users through RWAS <GO> and places the onchain data alongside the platform’s existing fixed-income, foreign exchange and money-market tools.

The Terminal is widely used by banks, asset managers and other financial professionals for real-time market data, news, analytics, trading and communications. Bloomberg has carried Bitcoin pricing on the platform since 2014 and currently provides pricing, reference data, identifiers and benchmarks for 50 cryptocurrencies.

The move comes as the stablecoin market capitalization has risen above $306 billion, according to DeFiLlama data, with Tether’s USDT accounting for roughly 60% of the market.
